Hi Lauren,

Thanks again for the call this morning. We ran the utilization exports overnight and I attached the 30/60/90-day token & GPU utilization snapshot. TL;DR: steady daytime load plus two daily peaks driven by batch inference jobs.

We’re at about 72% average GPU utilization across our Dedicated pool and see a repeated 2-hour window where latency-sensitive traffic spikes (p99 latency climbs and queued requests increase). We’re interested in a renewal but need a plan that:
- preserves our latency SLO during growth spikes;
- keeps committed spend aligned to baseline usage; and
- gives flexible burst capacity for predictable peaks.

Can you put together a staged top-up plan (tranches or burst corridor) that ties GPU add to actual utilization triggers? Also include any short-term credits if we agree to a 12→24 month commit.

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>

Samir — thanks for the data and the clear ask. I pulled the usage into our capacity model and sketched two options: a conservative steady-commit increase + burst corridor, and a staged tranching approach that adds capacity as utilization thresholds are met. High level:

Option A — Steady bump + managed burst:
- Immediate commit: +12 GPUs (NVIDIA H100 equiv) to cover daytime steady growth (expected headroom to 80% avg utilization).
- Burst corridor: add 8 GPUs reserved for 4x daily bursts (billed differently, lower commit).
- Early-renewal credit: 7% credit on MRR if you sign a 24-month extension within 30 days.

Option B — Utilization-triggered tranching (recommended):
- Phase 0 (current → baseline): no immediate commit. Add automated burst routing to existing capacity while enabling prefix KV cache for high-latency flows.
- Phase 1 (trigger when 72% 7-day rolling avg sustained for 10 days): reserve +6 GPUs.
- Phase 2 (trigger when 85% 7-day rolling avg sustained for 7 days or p99 latency > 150ms during peak): reserve additional +8 GPUs.
- Each tranche accompanied by a 30-day evaluation window and an optional short-term discounted topup for the first tranche.

Operational notes:
- We’ll instrument per-route telemetry and set up an alerting dashboard so your SREs see the utilization triggers before auto-commit executes.
- We can also enable a fallback to a compatible quantized model family if you prefer lower-cost burst alternatives.

I’m attaching a draft SOW for the tranching flow and a rough cost sketch. Ben — can you confirm pricing delta for the tranche discount tiers and a sample SLA addendum for the burst corridor?

Attachment: zenith-tranche-sow-draft.pdf (PDF, 220KB)

Cheers,
Lauren Bishop
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Lauren / Samir — quick pricing note (internal numbers simplified for thread):

Pricing assumptions for ZEN-4532 tranching:
- Baseline GPU unit price (H100 equiv) at current commit: $18,500 / GPU / month.
- Tranche discount tiers: tranche 1 (first +6 GPUs): 6% off baseline; tranche 2 (additional +8 GPUs): 9% off baseline (applies once tranche activated).
- Burst corridor: reserved standby at 40% of unit price (billed as "standby reserve") + metered per-token execution when used. This keeps committed spend lower while guaranteeing capacity.
- Early-renewal incentive: 7% credit across committed MRR for 24-month sign.

Operational prerequisites:
- Telemetry hooks and the utilization SLOs must be instrumented in the next 14 days for automatic tranche triggers to be reliable.
- Legal needs a one-page addendum for auto-commit triggers and evaluation windows (Ben to coordinate).

Samir — if you want, we can model expected monthly spend under the tranching plan vs. one-time larger commit. I can run a 12/18/24 month cashflow projection once you confirm which baseline scenario to compare.
